item.title: An Imgur Celebration
item.description:
Hi everyone, I'm MrPuckett I celebrated my 41st birthday this week, but that's not why I'm excited today
Every year around my birthday is another celebration right here on Imgur
Tomorrow we're celebrating the SEVEN YEAR anniversary of TheFreePizzaDude! Over 17,000 meals sent to people in need since 2019!
I always love celebrating milestones for this project because it forces me to remember where I came from
I started TheFreePizzaDude 7 years ago with almost nothing I moved to a small Tennessee town after being homeless with only a dog and one suitcase I don't own or have a single thing today from 7 years ago, sadly not even the dog.
While everything was changing and every year brought new challenges in sobriety and life, only one thing has remained constant for me since 2019 Every week a bunch of wholesome strangers on the internet join me to send meals to people who are struggling
Even though it's only one day a week, it's given me the structure and hope that I needed most of my life No matter how good or how bad a day I had, I was only ever a few days away from being back here with friends across the world
So I hope you'll join us again this week to celebrate how much love (and cheese) has been shared over the last 7 years Saturday, 2pm central, @TheFreePizzaDude, let's party.
17,000+ meals, 1,500+ grocery orders, 22 different foster and adopted dogs on the posts One big day to celebrate it all
I remember the exact day 7 years ago when I first started the project, how little hope I had for such a beautiful future Tomorrow we'll look to send as much food, and as much hope as we can to people in need. ... If you can't make the post but still want to help, you can always contribute to the Meal Fund to help others get fed - https://www.paypal.me/TheFreePizzaDude https://ko-fi.com/thefreepizzadude ... Saturday, 2pm central, let's spread some love.

item.title: GovBrief Today #560
item.description: For the first time since Roe v. Wade fell, a federal judge ruled the Constitution protects abortion in Idaho. Legislators there barred doctors from ending a pregnancy to save a woman who might take her own life. Mental health was the leading killer of Idaho's pregnant women, according to the state's own maternal mortality committee. The judge ruled that a woman has a constitutional right to an abortion when her pregnancy threatens her life or her health, and he blocked the state from prosecuting her doctors for performing one. The narrow ruling applies only to women in Idaho whose pregnancies endanger their bodies or their minds, and the state will most certainly appeal. But for three years, every federal courthouse said no constitutional right to abortion survived. Tonight a judge said one did.
